facts.text: The Kenya National Library Service started its camel library service in 1996 to serve nomadic herding communities in northeastern Kenya.
The camel library began in Garissa in 1996 and was extended to Wajir in 1999.
Motor vehicle libraries were not practical there because of poor roads and the herders' temporary settlements; trucks used as mobile libraries elsewhere in Kenya would get stuck.
Camels were the main means of transport in the region.
On a trip, one camel carried the books in two wooden boxes, one on each side of its hump; a second carried a tent; a third came along as a spare.
At each stop the books were laid out on mats inside the tent, and children borrowed them with library cards.
The service worked within a radius of about 15 kilometres of the libraries in town.
The camel library served readers from Monday to Thursday; from Friday to Sunday the camels were let out to feed and rest and were checked by vets for disease.
In 1999, most of the provincial library's books came from foreign aid, especially the charity Book Aid International.

notes: 每頭駱駝載書量各來源不同（約 400／500 本），文章不寫數字。
